meta.verdict: Of 297 BANKNIFTY option-buying strategies tested on 2016-2026 (daily ones at REAL NSE option prices, intraday ones with a premium model checked against real prices), none is statistically proven: 0 passed, 0 confirmed. Intraday option buying showed no edge at all - over 233 intraday strategies the index moved the bought option's way 49% of the time, a coin flip, and the typical one lost Rs245-322 a trade after costs. The ten below are the only distinct strategies that made money after every cost in BOTH 2016-2021 and 2022-2026. Nine are swing strategies held 1-7 sessions; most of their profit came from calls and from a handful of large winners. Simply holding calls LOST money in 2022-2026, so their timing did add something - but with 297 tried, part of this is luck. They run here on paper only, filled at the real order book, so a forward record can decide.
meta.selection_note: Chosen by the pre-registered protocol (backend/research/banknifty_2026_10/PROTOCOL.md) with one amendment made after the results and disclosed there: the 'three per family' rule counted all 48 library swing strategies as one family and would have stopped at six, so it was dropped; near-duplicates (daily P&L correlation above 0.7) are still removed, which took out mr_btst_finnifty (0.76 with wt_btst). Ranked by their 2022-2026 t-statistic. Tier C means positive in both periods but not statistically significant - the last four are barely positive after 2022. Click a row for its curve, its years and what it does at double spreads.

selected.label: Jesse Livermore: Pivotal Point Breakout
selected.description: From Livermore's 'Reminiscences of a Stock Operator' / 'How to Trade in Stocks': wait for a stock (or index) to build a base at a 'pivotal point,' then buy the breakout with conviction only once the level is cleanly cleared — no anticipation, no averaging down.
